$description: Every KinetixUI component and where it is really implemented. platformDefinitions is the ONE place a platform is declared — its family (web/native), label, abbreviation, whether its catalogue is complete, its declared PACKAGE maturity and how it is distributed. Package maturity is a product decision about the offering; how well each implementation is VERIFIED is a separate, derived value in verification.json, and the two must never be collapsed into one word. Everything downstream (platform-parity.json, component-status.json, the website, CI guardrails) derives from this file; nothing re-declares the platform list. categoryDefinitions is the ONE place the functional taxonomy is declared — its order is the order every surface lists categories in, and each entry carries the rule an assignment is judged against. Every component declares a category from that enum, a kind ('component' for a published API, 'recipe' for a documented composition with no export of its own) and optional facets; the website category map and the Storybook grouping are both generated from it, so neither can drift and no component can fall into a default category. A component lists only platforms whose source actually exists (that is what parity counts), and platformGuidance says what to show for every platform it is NOT on — a native equivalent, a composition, or a planned Angular wave — so no platform tab is ever blank or invented — scripts/check-platform-source.mjs verifies that against the packages.

Layout & Structure.rule: Arranges or contains other components and has no content of its own.

Forms & Inputs.rule: Collects a value from the user, or labels and structures the field that does.

Navigation.rule: Moves the user between places or levels.

Overlays.rule: Exists to present arbitrary content above the page.

Feedback & Status.rule: Reports state, progress, outcome or guidance.

Data Display.rule: Presents data the user reads rather than operates.

Media & Content.rule: Presents authored media or editorial content.

distribution.note: Also installable as source with `npx @kinetixui/cli add`.
Published from 0.24.0. Versions independently of @kinetixui/{tokens,ui,cli} — publication is distribution, not maturity, and Angular stays Preview.
publish-swiftui.yml splits packages/ui-swiftui to a mirror repo; it needs SWIFTUI_MIRROR_REPO and has never been run for real.
publish-compose.yml stages to the Central Portal; it needs four signing/credential secrets and defaults to a dry run.
publish-flutter.yml publishes to pub.dev; it needs PUB_DEV_CREDENTIALS and defaults to a dry run.

address-fields.lifecycleReason: New in the Phase 2 business foundations (business capability roadmap): the API has one consumer (the docs) and no product feedback yet, and its native and Angular adaptations are undecided, so the prop names may still change.
address-fields.platformNote: React-first business foundation (business capability roadmap, Phase 2 — docs/BUSINESS-CAPABILITY-ROADMAP.md). Roadmap target: Cross-platform Core. Native ports are an open roadmap decision, not a standing non-port: until one is made, each native tab shows the composition of existing Kinetix primitives that delivers the same outcome.

SwiftUI.reason: No native AddressFields yet. A Form Section of KinetixField + KinetixInput pairs in the product's own order, each with the matching .textContentType (.streetAddressLine1, .addressCity, .postalCode, …) for AutoFill.

Compose.reason: No native AddressFields yet. A Column of KinetixField + KinetixInput pairs in the product's own order, one per address part, with keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number on numeric parts. Autofill content types need a field that exposes semantics, which KinetixInput does not yet.

Flutter.reason: No native AddressFields yet. An AutofillGroup of TextField widgets in the product's own order, each with the matching AutofillHints (streetAddressLine1, addressCity, postalCode, …); KinetixInput has no autofill-hints parameter yet, so it cannot carry them.

SwiftUI.reason: No native AmountDisplay yet. Format with the product's FormatStyle (.currency(code:)), render Text with .monospacedDigit(), write the sign into the string, and give the Text an .accessibilityLabel with the full spoken amount.

Compose.reason: No native AmountDisplay yet. Format with the product's NumberFormat, render Text with fontFeatureSettings = "tnum", write the sign into the string, and give it a semantics contentDescription with the full spoken amount.

Flutter.reason: No native AmountDisplay yet. Format with the product's NumberFormat (intl), render Text with FontFeature.tabularFigures(), write the sign into the string, and wrap it in Semantics(label:) with the full spoken amount.

avatar-group.platformNote: standing non-port — the React component re-wraps its children, which no native layout system does; compose an Avatar row directly. Its cap and +N marker would port to a data-driven native API, so this is a scope decision rather than an impossibility

SwiftUI.reason: AvatarGroup's React implementation re-wraps each child to draw the ring, which is not how any native layout system composes — compose KinetixAvatar directly in an HStack / Row / Row of widgets with a negative offset. Note that the component's actual value, the `max` cap and the "+N" overflow marker, would port cleanly to a native API that takes a list instead of children; this stays a composition because that API has not been designed, not because the platform cannot express it.

SwiftUI.reason: No native DateRangeInput yet. Two DatePicker(displayedComponents: .date) fields (start, end) with the end's range starting at the chosen start, storing calendar dates as DateComponents, not Date instants.

direction-provider.platformNote: React-only by design: the web needs a provider to thread direction through Radix, while SwiftUI (environment .layoutDirection), Compose (LocalLayoutDirection) and Flutter (Directionality) already carry layout direction in the framework itself. Nothing to port.

Angular.reason: The web platform already threads direction: set dir on an element and every descendant inherits it, and Angular CDK's Directionality reads that same attribute. @kinetixui/angular has no Radix-style provider to thread it through, so there is nothing for a component to add.

SwiftUI.reason: SwiftUI carries layout direction in the environment. Set .environment(\.layoutDirection, .rightToLeft) and every view below reads it — there is no provider to port.

Compose.reason: Compose carries layout direction in a CompositionLocal. Provide LocalLayoutDirection and every composable below reads it — there is no provider to port.

Flutter.reason: Flutter carries layout direction in the widget tree. Wrap a subtree in Directionality and every widget below reads it — there is no provider to port.

Angular.reason: Angular ships its own form layer. ReactiveFormsModule gives the validation, state and submission handling that Form exists to wire up on React, and every @kinetixui/angular control implements ControlValueAccessor, so they bind to it directly. A KinetixUI form wrapper would be a second, worse form system.

SwiftUI.reason: Form is react-hook-form glue with no native analogue. KinetixField and the platform's own state hold the same job.

Compose.reason: Form is react-hook-form glue with no native analogue. KinetixField and the platform's own state hold the same job.

Flutter.reason: Form is react-hook-form glue with no native analogue. KinetixField and the platform's own state hold the same job.

notification-center.lifecycleReason: Product boundary unresolved. `unread` is a per-item flag with nothing owning the transition: `onMarkAllRead` has no item-level counterpart, so marking one notification read has no API. There is also no empty-state contract, and whether this belongs as a component or as a Block over Popover + List is an open question — see the PR C handoff.

SwiftUI.reason: No native PhoneInput yet. HStack of a KinetixSelect for the calling code and a KinetixInput with .keyboardType(.phonePad) and .textContentType(.telephoneNumber), with .environment(\.layoutDirection, .leftToRight) so the number reads left to right in an RTL layout.

Compose.reason: No native PhoneInput yet. Row of a KinetixSelectTrigger with KinetixSelectItem rows for the calling code and a KinetixInput with keyboardType = KeyboardType.Phone, inside CompositionLocalProvider(LocalLayoutDirection provides LayoutDirection.Ltr) so the number reads left to right in an RTL layout.

Flutter.reason: No native PhoneInput yet. Row of a KinetixSelect for the calling code and a TextField with keyboardType: TextInputType.phone and autofillHints: [AutofillHints.telephoneNumberNational] (KinetixInput has no keyboard-type parameter yet), inside Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.ltr) so the number reads left to right in an RTL layout.
